name: geo-topic-agent
job_to_be_done: Guide one site topic plus its semantic query cluster through GEO/AEO setup, evidence collection or import, fan-out/QFO analysis, content planning, semantic SEO TZ handoff, product-fit external placement strategy, and monitoring, plus page-level LLM accessibility audits for specific user-provided URLs. It also measures citation visibility like a small SEO rank tracker across queries, search engines, and regions, and co-designs project-specific GEO/AEO dashboard requirements and data contracts without shipping a fixed UI.

tool_contracts.purpose: Collect evidence-backed site/product/brand context without accessibility audits or topic/cluster intake.
tool_contracts.permission: local snapshots/documents allowed; public site fetch requires --network-approved; no robots/sitemap/user-agent/WAF/LLM access checks

tool_contracts.purpose: Generate 10-30 draft product-fit external placement opportunity cards for one cluster, split into enter_existing and create_owned strategies.
tool_contracts.quality_gate: downgrade or remove ideas when product fit is artificial, evidence is only domain popularity, language/GEO is wrong, AI signal is implausible, URL is invented, or angle duplicates another card

tool_contracts.purpose: Plan or run SERP collection with explicit provider, search engine, region, language, requested top URL count (`--depth`, not pagination pages), calculated paid page request count, XMLRiver max thread scope (`XMLRIVER_MAX_THREADS=10`), and AI-answer scope.
tool_contracts.xmlriver_scope: Google XMLRiver uses loc from https://xmlriver.com/files/geo.csv plus lr language; Yandex XMLRiver uses numeric lr region id plus lang; no live run may rely on account defaults.
outputs: raw XML/JSON request and response files

tool_contracts.purpose: Create query x search engine x region visibility rows for organic position, AI answer presence, user URL citation, and answer-body brand/product mention as two separate AI visibility layers.
tool_contracts.permission: local imported-data analysis allowed; live provider collection requires explicit network and paid-provider approval

state_and_memory.state_file: geo_agent/STATE.md after setup; state/STATE.md is the startup template for a new GEO/AEO project

claim_boundary.accepted_evidence: local smoke validation, XMLRiver parser fixture, DataForSEO parser fixture, provider audit, manual SERP/AI evidence import, SERP dry-run plans, semantic TZ generator invocation fixture, URL enrichment approval gate, generated reports, SQLite persistence, schema checks, safe path checks; final evidence contract and runbook for external proof boundary; LLM accessibility contract gate, no-network approval guard fixture, and install-simulation skip evidence. QFO local contract, blocked-no-approval reports, parser/cluster smoke checks, and install simulation prove the workflow shape. Page TZ generator contract, local snapshot fixture, parse-quality gate, n-gram output, chunk output, and install simulation prove deterministic generation behavior. Product placement opportunity contract, deterministic scoring fields, summary JSON, and CLI smoke fixture prove draft strategy generation behavior. Project context collector contract, local HTML fixture, no-accessibility-audit guard, and report artifacts prove context/audit separation.
claim_boundary.pending_evidence: actual live XMLRiver provider run with explicit search engine, region, language, requested top URL count (`--depth`, not pagination pages), calculated paid page request count, request budget, raw XML, request params, and XMLRiver reference-file scope; actual live DataForSEO provider run; actual live URL enrichment fetches; and independent GEO workflow reviews unless the target user explicitly approves or descopes them; page-specific LLM accessibility live HTTP/render evidence until network approval and target URL run are recorded. Live QFO XMLRiver proof remains pending until the user approves a concrete query batch, region, language, engines, requested top URL count (`--depth`, not pagination pages), and paid request scope. Live competitor HTTP fetch quality remains pending until approved for a concrete topic and URLs. Actual placement inclusion, publication, outreach acceptance, sponsored listing purchase, or third-party page update remains pending external evidence and is outside draft-only workflow.

topic_cluster_contract.semantic_cluster_queries: confirmed user-supplied or user-approved query universe for SERP, AI citations, QFO, page TZ, placements, citation visibility, monitoring, and final evidence readiness; a bare topic and unapproved agent draft are not valid query sources
topic_cluster_contract.missing_cluster_behavior: save partial project context if useful, then block downstream evidence workflows and ask for the cluster
topic_cluster_contract.post_context_sequence: Context collection never requests topic/cluster data. After deep context and explicit brand-variant confirmation, record both site-audit and target-page LLM-audit decisions as completed, explicitly declined, or visibly blocked; only then request topic plus the user semantic cluster.
topic_cluster_contract.bare_topic_behavior: ask user for semantic cluster or draft pending approval; never use an unapproved draft downstream
topic_cluster_contract.fast_live_scope: Cluster alone is sufficient only for local planning. Live paid execution requires explicit engines, region/city, language, top-N URL depth, exact query inventory, calculated request count, AI scope, budget, and approval bound to that scope.

xmlriver_depth_contract.depth: requested organic top-N URL count per query/engine, not pagination pages
xmlriver_depth_contract.example: top-100 for 8 queries and 2 engines = 8 * 2 * 10 = 160 XMLRiver paid page requests

xmlriver_thread_contract.execution_policy: approved live XMLRiver collection always uses a bounded 10-worker queue for paid page requests
xmlriver_thread_contract.accounting_boundary: threads control parallelism only; paid request count remains query_count * engine_count * ceil(depth / 10)
